findings.title: Google Calendar credential key is overwritten with a Zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full `SafeParseReturnType` object (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), whereas `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` previously returned the unwrapped credential object. Passing that wrapper directly to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` stores `{ success: true, data: { ... } }` in `credential.key`. On the next instantiation of `GoogleCalendarService`, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` on line 75 will fail because the top-level keys (`access_token`, `refresh_token`, etc.) are now nested under `data`, breaking Google Calendar for the user after the first token refresh.

findings.title: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses `[z.string().toString()]` as literal property keys and strips unknown fields
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` do not define index signatures in Zod; they evaluate `.toString()` on the schema object (producing `"[object Object]"`) and register a literal property with that name requiring a `number` (overwritten by `z.unknown().optional()`). Because `z.object` strips unrecognised keys by default, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` strips every field except `access_token` (including `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, `refresh_token`, etc.). When credential syncing is enabled, callers like Office365 and Zoom receive `undefined` for the expiry field, leading to `NaN` expiry dates or broken credentials.

findings.title: `prisma` is not imported, `refreshOAuthTokens` is not used, and refreshed token is not passed to jsforce
findings.body: Three issues in `SalesforceCalendarService.getClient`: (1) `prisma.credential.update` is called on line 96, but `prisma` is never imported in this file, causing a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime; (2) the token refresh `fetch` on line 75 is called directly instead of through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so Salesforce credentials are never synced via `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` and every `getClient` call unconditionally hits Salesforce's token endpoint; (3) lines 105-107 still pass `credentialKey.access_token` (the old token) instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` when constructing `new jsforce.Connection(...)`.

findings.title: Return type mismatch between `fetch` in `refreshOAuthTokens` and Google/HubSpot/Zoho callers
findings.body:
`refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` object when `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is enabled, but returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns when disabled. Several callers expect library-specific return shapes instead of a `fetch` `Response`:
- `GoogleCalendarService` (line 94) reads `res?.data` (an axios/gaxios response property), which is `undefined` on a `fetch` `Response`, causing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'access_token')`.
- `HubspotCalendarService` (`packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177`) expects a parsed `HubspotToken` object (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn`, `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken`), which do not exist on a `fetch` `Response`.
- `BiginCalendarService` (`packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:96`) and `ZohoCrmCalendarService` (`packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:217`) expect an Axios response with `.data`, which is `undefined` on a `fetch` `Response`.

findings.title: `credentialId` is passed instead of `credential.userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens`
findings.body: `refreshAccessToken` passes `credentialId` (the primary key of the `Credential` row) as the third argument (`userId`) to `refreshOAuthTokens`. When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` sends this value as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint, requesting tokens for the wrong user ID.

findings.title: Webex token refresh does not use `parseRefreshTokenResponse`
findings.body: `webexAuth` calls `refreshOAuthTokens` on line 62, but still validates the response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse(responseBody)` on line 88 instead of `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. When `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is used and returns only the minimum token response (access token and expiry), `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` fails validation because `scope`, `token_type`, `refresh_token`, and `refresh_token_expires_in` are required.

findings.title: Sync webhook stores raw `keys` without setting `refresh_token` fallback required by app schemas
findings.body: When credentials are created or updated via `/api/webhook/app-credential`, the decrypted `keys` payload from the parent application (which according to the PR only needs to provide the access token and expiry) is written directly to `prisma.credential` without ensuring a `refresh_token` placeholder is present or transforming `expires_in` to `expiry_date`. Integrations such as `GoogleCalendarService` (`googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)`) and `ZoomVideoApiAdapter` (`zoomTokenSchema.parse(credential.key)`) parse `credential.key` before calling `refreshAccessToken` and require `refresh_token: z.string()` (and for Zoom, `scope`, `token_type`, `expiry_date`), so initial parsing of synced credentials will fail before any refresh can occur.
